This work investigates the evolving security relationship between Japan and ASEAN amidst a global shift from unipolarity to multipolarity, driven by challenges such as China's rise, North Korean nuclear activity, and the Russia-Ukraine war. A second thesis from 2024, titled "INDOMALPHI Trilateral Cooperative Arrangement to Combat Piracy and Armed Robbery Against Ships: Towards Greater Cooperation and Security," covers the sub-topics of cybersecurity and privacy and business and entrepreneurship. This study examines the effectiveness of the Trilateral Cooperative Arrangement (TCA) between Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines in combating piracy, armed robbery, and maritime kidnapping in the Sulu-Celebes Sea. The third thesis, supervised in 2023, is titled "Minilateralism Shaping ASEAN Centrality: The Case of Sulu-Sulawesi Seas Patrol." This work focuses on the sub-topic of governance and public policy and examines how small-group collaborations interact with ASEAN centrality regarding Southeast Asian maritime security, specifically focusing on the Sulu-Sulawesi Sea.
